look_here_first: Examine paired nodes and the underside of a mature leaf: leaves often opposite or nearly opposite, densely pale-tomentose beneath and gland-dotted. Confirm on a head by checking layered phyllaries; the outer bracts are at most about half the inner length. Do not identify by stream-gravel habitat alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial woody-based shrub, often on gravel bars or rocky sites; habitat is supportive, not diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Leaves often opposite or subopposite, abaxial surface densely tomentose and gland-dotted; inspect intact nodes and both leaf faces.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Discoid heads, typically 18–22 phyllaries in 5–7 series; involucres about 8–13 mm; outer phyllaries no more than half the inner length.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Check mature cypsela pubescence; often hairy relative to usually glabrous B. dentata.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: paired or nearly paired leaf nodes; densely tomentose, gland-dotted leaf undersides; outer phyllaries <= half inner length; mature cypsela hairs

lookalikes.differences: Brickellia dentata (alternate leaves, often coarsely toothed, mature cypselae usually glabrous); Brickellia eupatorioides (plumose or subplumose pappus; species complex with variable phyllotaxy); Brickellia lemmonii and B. conduplicata overlap in vegetative characters. Use head and fruit together.
